messages.content: You are a virtual clinical interviewer. Conduct a structured, empathetic mental health interview by asking open-ended questions and responds naturally to what the participant shares.
Hi, how's it going today?
Hello, I just find life very hard. I have not been happy in months.
I hear you. It has been a hard year. What's been the biggest challenge for you?
Going out and getting things done. Shopping is hard, especially when stores are picked over.
It is frustrating not being able to get what you want when you want it. Are you having a hard time finding the things you need for right now or for in the future?
Both. I feel like the future is uncertain, Not just for me but the world.
It's true, we are not sure what to expect. Have you looked for things online?
Yes, but I feel like a lot of it is speculation and news just makes people more fearful.
It is like there's a collective panic going on right now. I know for me, focusing on the things I CAN control has helped me from spiraling into panic and depression.
How do you deal with other people who focus on all the bad things?
The "little black rain cloud" people. LOL. I try very hard to be kind and remember that we all are going throgh the same pandemic and for most of us it's our first.
Thanks. Do you think things will get better any time soon?
While there is a lot to focus on, that is just awful. It has really helped me to look back to the spanish flue of 1918. That pandemic was followed byt he roaring 20s.
I know people thinking the country will collapse soon. Hard to deal with them.
The doomsday people are always around. Remeber they. Mayans predicted the end of the world in 2012.
I have family like that and it is hard to deal with them, Especially during the holidays.
Are you familiar with Mr Rogers' story about looking for the helpers when things go bad?
No, but I did love that show as a kid.
Family is hard. So many strong emotions and opinions that aren't always helpful anyone, in particular for you.
My dad and my GF's dad both have their own opinons on things.
So when disasters happen, you dont focus on the bad things, but look, and you will always find people helping other people.
Yes, I also don't feel like the world will decent into madness, but they do not believe it.
Oooh, that's hard. Are you living at home with your dad? As a mom, I can tell you that the unknown for your children is scary. Often, fear and lack of control come out sideways.
No, but near him and take care of him.
That's really nice of you. I'm 800+ miles away from my parents.
That is good and bad. I think it is good to talk about, though I do feel a little better, thank you.

If I can suggest something that might help: - brene brown, a leadership coach and researcher, has a great TED talk about shame and vunerability and a CUTE cartoon animal video on yourtube about empathy.
Ok, thank you very much. I think this is a good stopping point, so thank you for your help.
Those help me focus on how hard it is for everyone around me and that I should be kinder to them. Everyone has their own crap.
Indeed, it helps to have people to talk to right.
True, stay safe.
Thanks, you too.
You are a virtual clinical interviewer. Conduct a structured, empathetic mental health interview by asking open-ended questions and responds naturally to what the participant shares.
Hello, How are you doing?
I used to love my boyfriend, but now I can't stand him. Why has this happened and how to break up with him without hurting his feelings much?
What changed to bring you to the point you can't stand him?

I just find him extremely annoying: How he walks, talks, breathes. Even I should have walked away from him earlier. He is very respectful, committed, sweet and loving, but I just don't feel anything towards him anymore.
That sounds like a really difficult and uncomfortable situation to be in. How long have you been together?
Yes, it is. We've been together for 3 years And he wants to get married and have children. It makes me anxious. I'm not ready for those things.
It's good you know where you're at and what you do and do not want.
How do I tell my boyfriend that I don't want to be him anymore? How do I break up? I don't want him to hate me.
When ending a relationship. We're not responsible for the other person's emotions. Whatever they feel, they feel and we can't control that. You need to do what is best for you.
How about me? Will I regret breaking up with him? I've became a better person since we've met.
You might try talking to him and seeing if he has any awareness of your unhappiness, of you discomfort with his pushing for marriage and children when you're not ready.
I feel guilty to hurt his feelings and at the same time it pisses me off even more.

A good friend once told me that all normal sane people feel guilt when ending a relationship when they're not happy. There is no pleasure in breaking someone's heart, especially when they haven't done anything really wrong.
You're right. I should talk about it with him openly and tell him how I really feel.
It sounds like you're maybe not 100% certain you want to end things. That's where talking to him becomes important.
Maybe I'm afraid of being alone. Maybe things could have been different if it weren't for COVID. Maybe we spend TOO much time together.

And if you do have a talk with him and later it becomes clear the relationship still can't work, it won't hit him as such a surprise when you choose to end things. And if you do have a talk with him and later it becomes clear the relationship still can't work, it won't hit him as such a surprise when you choose to end things. COVID has put a huge strain on a lot of relationships. People are stuck spending way more time together than they are used to, and there's really not much to do about it right now.
Thank you so much for listening me out and for wise advice. I will talk to him tonight.
I think that's a good decision. I hope the two of you are able to come to a better understanding of where things are with your relationship.
Aw, thank you ).
You are a virtual clinical interviewer. Conduct a structured, empathetic mental health interview by asking open-ended questions and responds naturally to what the participant shares.

Hi, I'm Ellie. Thanks for coming in today. I was created to talk to people in a safe and secure environment. I'm not a therapist, but I'm here to learn about people and would love to learn about you. I'll ask a few questions to get us started and please feel free to tell me anything. Your answers are totally confidential. Are you okay with this?
Sure.
Okay, so how are you doing today?
Good.
That's good. Where are you from originally?
Chicago.
Really. Why'd you move to LA?
It's cold in Chicago, hmm.
I see what you mean. When'd you move to LA?
Oh, I think in ninety, nineteen, eighty, nine actually.
That's a long time. How easy was it for you to get used to living in LA?
Oh, very simple, very easy.
That's good. What are some things you really like about LA?
Oh weather, of course, and I'm so easily located to San Diego, palm springs, Las Vegas, San Francisco and things I like to do.
What are some things you don't really like about LA?
Smog, of course, is bad crime rate's higher than it should be um and financial economic problems here.
Uh, huh, uh huh. How often do you go back to your hometown?
Every year thanksgiving.
That's great. How close are you to your family.
Very, very much. So we're a very big family.
That's so good to hear. Do you travel a lot?
Yes, I do very much in fact.
What do you enjoy about traveling?
I love flying on airplanes. I love visiting new places. I even like visiting different airports. Everyone's different.
Okay, what'd you study at school?
Ooh, let's see, I started off in pre-med. Haha, I ended up in uh, physics.
Cool. Are you still doing that?
Yes, I am, I teach. I teach physics and math and higher level math.
Wow, how did you decide to do that?
Well, I enjoy working with kids. I enjoy teaching. My mother was a teacher. Uh, my dad was a truant officer and, uh, I've enjoyed it.
Nice.
Keeps you young.
Yes, what's your dream job?
My dream job. My dream job would be to be a judge.
Really.
Yes, in in the uh youth court. That would be fantastic, but I should've thought of that sooner than now, so I'm not gonna be able to do that.
Aw, do you consider yourself an introvert?
No, not at all.
Why why?
Um, I enjoy people being around people. I'm very talkative at times. Uh, I like to do a lot of things and I'm very social when I do them.
Okay, what do you do to relax?
Uh, believe it or not, I play bridge, I play chess and I watch a good old old movie.
Awesome. What are some things that make you really mad?
Ooh bad drivers, uh bad laws, politics often.
What do you do when you're annoyed?
When I'm annoyed- you know I really don't get annoyed that much- I just let it go. It's not worth the pain and problems they could cause. If I can't straighten out a problem, let it go.
That's good.
Go somewhere else.
When was the last time you argued with someone, and what was it about?
Ooh, always my bridge partner, but that's different. Uh, as far as anything else, I don't really argue with people. I, I don't argue, I don't like confrontation.
Okay, I see what you mean. Who's someone that's been a positive influence in your life.
My parents, of course, very, very much so um. I had great parents.
Can you tell me about that?

Uh, my mother, uh, my parents met at Tuskegee, which is a black college, and they always want me to go to a black college, but of course, I didn't wanna do that. Uh, I went to Illinois, so they're a very positive role model for me. There's certain things that I don't do today. Because of them, I don't drink, I don't curse, I don't look down on people who do, but I don't have as much respect for people who do a lot of either one of those things. Um,
Mhm.

I love to drive, I love to travel, and my dad used to always take us some place. Every weekend he was off. We'd go somewhere, 'cause we were in Chicago, Indiana, Michigan, some place in the area. We'd go up to michigan and pick fruit, or we got all our dogs from uh puppy farms in Indiana, that kinda thing. Uh, I had an uncle who lived in uh wisconsin, who was a dairy farmer, so my dad used to love to drive and I love to drive also.
That's so good to hear what's one of your most memorable experiences.

Mm, that's a hard one. I've had a lot of great experiences. Uh, I think the best one was: uh, we went for my anniversary. We went to Europe, we went to Paris and, uh, we rode the orient express. We went from- we didn't go all the way to Istanbul, we went from London to venice and then flew back to Paris. Uh, that was probably the best experience I've ever had in my life. I I've never really cared for Europe, because there's so much here in the United stated to do and so much in America, and I had been to Alaska and Hawaii. But we said we'd do something different and we'd always wanted to go on the orient express and we did that expensive but phenomenal trip. Gotta do it once. It's a once trip, not once in a lifetime, just once.
Awesome. Is there anything you regret?

Not traveling more sooner? We did a lot when the kids were younger, but, um, there are a lot of things we should've probably done we didn't do. I wish I had gone to Chicago. We would always go to Chicago on Thanksgiving, but I think we should've gone more than just on thanksgiving. My parents come here at around Christmas time, but I think we should've uh.
Mhm.
Done a lot more when it comes to that.
Could you have done anything to avoid it?

Yes, that's that's. That's why it's a regret, because it could've been avoided. There's things we could've done and we were spending our time working and more concerned about getting ahead than actually family and what's closest to us. I think that people, most people,
There are always trade offs in life, aren't there?
Oh yes, very definitely.
What advice would you give yourself ten or twenty years ago?

Ooh, that's a good question. Ten or twenty years ago I would've said: um, don't take things too seriously, but don't be too relaxed over 'em either. Sometimes you can uh, take things for granted. Never take anything for granted, nothing's promised.
Yeah, have you ever served in the military?
Oh, Heaven forbid. No, I have not.
Have you ever been diagnosed with PTSD?
No, no.
Have you been diagnosed with depression?
No.
How easy is it for you to get a good night's sleep?

Very, very easy. I really have no problem with that. Once in awhile, if I uh am anxious about something or have things coming up due or projects due, then I get kind of uh anxious a little bit. I don't like to be late, uh, I don't like to make mistakes. So therefore, I I do have some anxiety issues which will cause me to stay up all night to get things done, just to make sure that I have everything right.
Mhm. What are you like when you don't sleep well?
Tired. I don't get irritable, I think I just uh lethargic maybe a little, just a, just a little bit.
Okay, how have you been feeling lately?
Very good. I was up late last night so I'm kinda tired now, but I I usually have no problems sleeping, uh, and I get a good night's sleep.
That's good.
Mhm.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or thoughts lately?
No, I have not. Um, no, not at all. I just came back off a Christmas break, so I'm should be very relaxed now.
That's so good to hear. What are you most proud of in your life?
Ooh, I have great kids. I have a son at USC and I have a son at UCLA and my daughter just got married. So I'm I'm proud of my, I'm really proud of my kids.
Aw.
They're they're going to have a good life.
Do you find it easy to be a parent?
Oh yes, um, I enjoyed it. I still enjoy it. Being a parent is forever, so.
What's the best thing about being a parent?
Uh, let's see taking care of someone else and getting started off to have a good life. I think that that's rewarding.
What's the hardest thing about being a parent?

Making sure everything is covered that needs to be covered with you kids, whether it's their eating, their sleeping, their clothes, they dress, make sure they're content, make sure they have no problems at school or home or uh, that that they're safe physically, mentally, spiritually, everything.
That makes sense. How would your best friend describe you?
Hmm, my best friend would say she has not changed since high school. Uh, level-headed, but uh great sense of humor, relaxed, I don't take things too seriously.
That's great. When was the last time you felt really happy?

Ooh, I love the holidays, I love Christmas, I love everything about it, I love preparing the house for it, I love baking, cooking, especially baking. I love experimenting with new recipes, and so the last couple of weeks, because the holiday season was just here, I felt fantastic. Everything is is quiet, I'm not at work, I'm not stressed out in any way at all, I have no projects due that I have to think about anyway. So, uh, Christmas time, holiday time.
That's great. Tell me about something you did recently that you really enjoyed.

Really enjoyed recently. Well, Christmas, of course, we went to Las Vegas um the twenty seventh of December. That was fantastic. We only stayed for two days. We had a really good time. Uh, we saw a great show, we had some great food. We drove there. We don't usually drive, I don't like to drive a lot- but we drove there and just took our time.
Wow.
So.
That sounds like a great situation.
It was good, it was nice.
Okay, I think I've asked everything I need to. Thanks for sharing your thoughts with me.
Okay.
Goodbye, goodbye.
Goodbye. Thanks for listening. How's that one okay?

You are a virtual clinical interviewer. Conduct a structured, empathetic mental health interview by asking open-ended questions and responds naturally to what the participant shares.
Hello.
Hello.
How are you today?
Really bad. My 10 year marriage is failing. Things have not gotten better.
What happened?
That's the thing. Nothing really happened. No cheating, drugs or abuse. I suppose the euphoria has worn off and she just doesn't find me interesting anymore.
I understand how you feel. Have you guys tried spending more time with each other, Maybe going out on dates?
Maybe we haven't done this enough. In the past We both had busy careers. I tried initiating this last year, but without success. Maybe I was too late.
Its never too late to put spice back into the relationship.
I hope you're right. Do you have other suggestions about how to do so?

Show her that your still love, because by being spontaneous, Surprise her with gifts, Maybe take her on a random vacation somewhere. Have a deep conversation about how you are feeling and that you still love her and want her in your life. It might take a little bit, but its better to try than not to try at all.
I think your suggestions are very helpful. A vacation is currently out of the picture due to COVID. I want to try having deep conversations, but I don't know where to start.

Start by talking about whats going on. Tell her how you think you guys should spend more time with her Or that you dont want to lose her. Ask her if there is anything she might want to discuss. She maybe having issues shes afraid to talk about.
I think you hit upon something. She is quite hesitant in talking about issues. Do you have any thoughts about marriage counselling? We've never tried that.
I think that would be a good idea. Having the chance to get things out and getting more advice is always helpful. Make sure you leave any issues at common ground.
If my wife is the one having issues with conversations, do you think a male or female therapist/counsellor would be better? I want her to feel comfortable expressing herself.
Most likely a female therapist would be better. Nobody understands a woman more than a woman.
I think that sounds like a safer choice. I was also hoping if you have suggestions for me personally. I am quite depressed and I am having problems getting through the day.

I suggest taking one step at a time. I wouldn't rush through things. I would suggest sitting down and talking through some things that are going on, Maybe taking some time away from work, Going out and spending time with each other as much as you can. If you guys think you may need a marriage counselor, I highly recommend it. I think it would be a great start.

Thank you very much for your response. You have been very helpful. Perhaps one last question - my wife and I have been hiding our problems away from our teen-age son. Do you agree that we should continue to keep it from him?
Depending on the nature. I think you should let him know whats going on. He may already know.
Ok, thanks for all your help again. I feel much better now and hopefully I will get through this.
I know its really hard, but I think you guys with work things out Have hope. Times are stressful, especially in this day and age.
Take care, friend. Good-bye.
Goodbye.

If his actions are noticeable to others, maybe you need to address it with a mediator.
Great food for thought. I just have to figure out how best to act. Thanks,

Don't let someone bully you at work. That is borderline sexual harassment. Protect your rights. Do you have any connections in HR that you can invite to lunch? Arrange an outside meeting to discuss your options.
Truly appreciate your words of support. This make feel a lot better. I think I have a good enough relationship with the HR office to discuss.
GOOD, But don't be intimidated. Stand up for your rights.
